RagShortTexts: Hymetius used and replenished public grain; surplus funds and authority led to proceedings.

Variants.Content: As proconsul of Africa, Hymetius used public grain to ease a shortage and replenished the store after prices fell, leaving a surplus. He paid part of the difference to the treasury but faced proceedings, later enlarged by private writings and religious accusations. Grain, proceeds and authority were all disputed.

For hungry people, releasing stores could bring immediate relief. Authorization and the recording of proceeds affected whether the official could continue. Receiving food and hearing a verdict were different kinds of news.

An official had to account for stock, sale proceeds, replacement purchases and the balance. The case also entangled accounts with letters, informers and appeal: scrutiny was not dispensable, but accusation was not conviction.
